Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Patches and DLC as zip files**: the game loads `patch.zip`, `patch2.zip` and so on from next to it and then from its save folder, after the `patch.xp3` archives, so a patch reaches the web, Android and iOS builds too. A zip can hold its files in `data/`'s layout, and `KAGMountPatchZip(storage)` mounts DLC while the game runs
- **kagex-release builds patches**: every build writes a list of its files, and a later build given that list (Output > *Patch from*) writes `patch.zip` with what changed since. A patch alone needs no platform or engine packages
- **CLIP STUDIO PAINT layers as images**: `clip://name.clip/root/folder/layer.bmp` on KAG and World layers, on every platform (the clipfile plugin's own route only worked on Windows)
- The sample's KAGEX Extended Layer demo ends with its emblem as two layers of one `.clip` file, turning separately
- The web, Android and iOS builds gained the minizip and clipfile plugins
- kagex-release keeps a `.clip` or `.psd` file that a script loads layers from, though the default exclusions match it
- kagex-release 0.7.0 downloads the 0.7.0 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.7.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
